No, that statement is not accurate.

Here’s the clarification:

- **EU/EEA/Swiss citizens** have the right to **freedom of movement** within the EU and can live and work in any EU country without needing a permit for stays up to 90 days. For longer stays (more than 90 days), they may need to register their residence but **they do not automatically receive a C permit** after five years.

- The **"C permit" (Permis C)** is a **Swiss immigration document**, not an EU-wide one. It is issued by Switzerland to **third-country nationals** (non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens) who have lived legally in Switzerland for an extended period, typically after holding a B permit (short- or long-term residence permit) for several years.

- EU citizens moving to Switzerland do **not** get a C permit after five years. Instead, they may be eligible for **long-term residence** status (under the terms of the **Free Movement Agreement** between Switzerland and the EU), but this is not the same as a Swiss C permit.

In short, the C permit is specific to Switzerland, and EU citizens do not automatically receive it after five years in any EU country. Their rights depend on the specific country they are living in and the national immigration rules of that country.
